Messages.Author: Alec Chang
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 15 Nov 1996 11:00:41 -0800, Wot...@aol.com (Jon Wilkie)
wrote:

>In article <01bbd246$dbd91000$a2166bc7@Tom>, "Steven Bucy"
><tb...@lainet.com> wrote:
>
>> Here is a old one that I don't know if we have ever had a official ruling
>> on.
>> Do Raven and Camille Devereux contest?
>
>Do they have the same name? Well, I guess they don't contest! :) I have
>both in my deck (all-female Ride of the Valkyries theme deck).

Mmm... The problem here is that by this ruling, the Gangrel get a
boost by having two vampires with exactly the same statistics. The
Giovanni have this in Mario and Cristophero Giovanni, but the effect
on the game is less as
a) there are less Giovanni total in all card sets,
and
b) Camille/Raven is a _very_ good vampire for gangrel decks. Being
able to have two copies of her/them in play not only makes Gangrel
decks more powerful in play(not too obviously, but it does), it also
gives Gangrel decks more options in terms of vampires in-clan than any
other clan than the Toreador(who have Marianna Gilbert, who I have not
seen yet due to my laziness in not mailing off for her....sigh...).
Not only that, but Raven is, as I mentioned earlier, very good for the
gangrel if not _the_ best vampire that they have, for economy of cost,
speed, and discipline combinations.

I'm not saying that having them contest is necessary for game balance,
but giving the Gangrel an advantage for a random reason(ie, Camille
Devereax was copied off of a victoria's secret catalog picture, and
had to be withdrawn and replaced by Raven- dang it's nice to have
obsessive artist friends sometimes....) instead of for a concious game
balance reason seems to be, well, a bit too lax. Just because a card
or minor effect doesn't have a visibly unbalancing effect on the game,
that doesn't mean that it isn't unbalancing it, and from a theoretical
standpoint, that's what this ruling does.

Alec Chang
